scope: Corollary 5.3 (Domination of the deletion-line law) of the manuscript “Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders” (preprints/Balanced-Counterexamples-to-Rysers-Conjecture-at-Prime-Orders-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 162 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5be7cf2d1f382e80), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D consist of the selected split lines and the lines M1 g in the preceding experiment. Conditional on A, the law of D is dominated pointwise by exp(O(q)) times the uniform law on sets containing three distinct lines in each direction.
